subproblem.title: Vanishing of ∫Dφ[v]dν on a set of directions extends to its span
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, ν a Borel measure on ℝ^P with ν(K) < ∞ for every compact K, φ : ℝ^P → ℝ a C^∞ function with compact support, and S ⊆ ℝ^P a set of vectors such that ∫Dφ(y)[v]dν(y) = 0 for every v ∈ S. Then ∫Dφ(y)[v]dν(y) = 0 for every v in the linear span of S.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (φ : Euclid P → ℝ) (S : Set (Euclid P)), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ν K < ∞) → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) φ → HasCompactSupport φ → (∀ v ∈ S, ∫ y, fderiv ℝ φ y v ∂ν = 0) → ∀ v ∈ Submodule.span ℝ S, ∫ y, fderiv ℝ φ y v ∂ν = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5(ii)–(iii) of the parent proof (linearity of v ↦ ∫Dψ(y)[v]dν(y), justified by integrability of the continuous compactly supported integrands against a measure finite on compact sets, and its vanishing on the span of the generators), stated for an arbitrary set S of directions.
Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P; Dφ(y) = fderiv ℝ φ y, a continuous linear functional on ℝ^P; C^∞ means ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (in the contract scope ∞ is ENNReal's, so the order is written (⊤ : ℕ∞)); for v ∈ ℝ^P let g_v(y) := Dφ(y)[v] and I(v) := ∫ g_v dν.
1. (ν is finite on compacts.) The hypothesis ν(K) < ∞ for every compact K is precisely the defining property of IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts ν, so this instance is available.
2. (Each g_v is integrable.) Fix v. Since φ is C^∞, hence C^1, the map y ↦ Dφ(y) is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv, using 1 ≤ ∞), and evaluating at the fixed vector v shows that g_v is continuous (Continuous.clm_apply with a constant). Since φ has compact support, g_v has compact support (HasCompactSupport.fderiv_apply: g_v vanishes outside the compact set tsupport φ). A continuous compactly supported function is integrable with respect to a measure that is finite on compact sets (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport, with step 1); hence g_v is ν-integrable.
3. (I is linear.) Because each Dφ(y) is linear, g_{x+x'}(y) = g_x(y) + g_{x'}(y), g_{c•x}(y) = c·g_x(y) and g_0(y) = 0 for all y (map_add, map_smul, map_zero). By step 2 and linearity of the integral on integrable functions, I(x + x') = I(x) + I(x') (integral_add) and I(c•x) = c·I(x) (integral_const_mul); also I(0) = ∫0 dν = 0.
4. (Induction over the span.) Let v ∈ span S. We prove I(v) = 0 by induction on membership in the span (Submodule.span_induction): (generators) if v ∈ S then I(v) = 0 by hypothesis; (zero) I(0) = 0 by step 3; (sums) if I(x) = 0 and I(x') = 0 then I(x + x') = I(x) + I(x') = 0 by step 3; (scalar multiples) if I(x) = 0 then I(c•x) = c·I(x) = 0 by step 3. Hence ∫Dφ(y)[v]dν(y) = I(v) = 0 for every v ∈ span S. ∎

subproblem.title: The cycle condition tested on φα gives ∫Dφ[v]dν = 0 for a Riesz vector v of α
subproblem.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, ν a Borel measure on ℝ^P, ζ₀ ∈ Λ_{d+1}(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P (d+1)), α a d-covector, v ∈ ℝ^P and φ : ℝ^P → ℝ a C^∞ function with compact support. Assume (i) ∫ζ₀(dψ(y))dν(y) = 0 for every test d-form ψ ∈ TestFormOn univ d, where dψ := exteriorDerivative ψ, and (ii) ζ₀(γ) = ⟨v, w⟩ whenever w ∈ ℝ^P and γ is a (d+1)-covector with γ(u) = Σ_{i=0}^{d} (−1)^i⟨w, u_i⟩α(Fin.removeNth i u) for all u. Then ∫Dφ(y)[v]dν(y) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (ζ₀ : MultiVector P (d + 1)) (α : Covector (Euclid P) d) (v : Euclid P) (φ : Euclid P → ℝ), (∀ ψ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) d, ∫ y, ζ₀ (exteriorDerivative (ψ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) y) ∂ν = 0) → (∀ (w : Euclid P) (γ : Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1)), (∀ u : Fin (d + 1) → Euclid P, γ u = ∑ i : Fin (d + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (i : ℕ) * (inner ℝ w (u i) * α (i.removeNth u))) → ζ₀ γ = inner ℝ v w) → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) φ → HasCompactSupport φ → ∫ y, fderiv ℝ φ y v ∂ν = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3, 4 and 5(i) of the parent proof (the test form ψα, the identity d(ψα)(y) = (∇ψ(y))^♭∧α, and ∫Dψ(y)[v_α]dν(y) = ∫ζ₀(d(ψα)(y))dν(y) = 0), with the Riesz vector v_α replaced by an arbitrary vector v having its defining property (hypothesis (ii) below). Uses the sibling extderiv_smul (accepted dgcr_bwd_extDeriv_smul_const): for a : ℝ^P → ℝ differentiable at x and a constant m-covector β, exteriorDerivative (y ↦ a(y)•β) x u = Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i·(Da(x)(u_i)·β(removeNth i u)) for all u.
Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P with real inner product ⟨·,·⟩; Dφ(y) = fderiv ℝ φ y; C^∞ means ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞); a test d-form ψ ∈ TestFormOn univ d is a d-form ψ : ℝ^P → Covector (Euclid P) d with IsTestForm ψ (IsSmoothForm ψ, i.e. ContDiff ℝ ∞ ψ, and HasCompactSupport ψ) and tsupport ψ ⊆ univ (membership in testFormOnSubmodule univ d). Hypotheses: (i) ∫ζ₀(dψ(y))dν(y) = 0 for every test d-form ψ; (ii) ζ₀(γ) = ⟨v, w⟩ whenever w ∈ ℝ^P and γ is a (d+1)-covector with γ(u) = Σ_i (−1)^i·(⟨w, u_i⟩·α(removeNth i u)) for all u : Fin (d+1) → ℝ^P; φ is C^∞ with compact support.
1. (The test form φα.) Let ω(y) := φ(y)•α. It is C^∞ as the product of the C^∞ scalar function φ with the constant covector α (ContDiff.smul with contDiff_const); it has compact support because ω(y) = 0 whenever φ(y) = 0 (HasCompactSupport.smul_right); and tsupport ω ⊆ univ trivially. Hence ω ∈ TestFormOn univ d.
2. (The hypothesis on ω.) By (i) applied to ψ := ω: ∫ζ₀(dω(y))dν(y) = 0.
3. (Pointwise identity ζ₀(dω(y)) = Dφ(y)[v].) Fix y ∈ ℝ^P. Since φ is C^∞ it is differentiable at y. Let g := (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ ℝ^P).symm (Dφ(y)) be the gradient of φ at y; by the Riesz representation, ⟨g, h⟩ = Dφ(y)(h) for every h (InnerProductSpace.toDual_symm_apply). By extderiv_smul with m = d, a = φ, β = α, x = y, for every u: dω(y)(u) = Σ_i (−1)^i·(Dφ(y)(u_i)·α(removeNth i u)) = Σ_i (−1)^i·(⟨g, u_i⟩·α(removeNth i u)). So γ := dω(y) satisfies the formula of (ii) with w := g, and (ii) gives ζ₀(dω(y)) = ⟨v, g⟩ = ⟨g, v⟩ (symmetry of the real inner product, real_inner_comm) = Dφ(y)(v).
4. (Conclusion.) By step 3 the functions y ↦ Dφ(y)[v] and y ↦ ζ₀(dω(y)) coincide at every y, so their integrals with respect to ν coincide (integral_congr_ae applied to an everywhere-true equality; no integrability is needed). Therefore ∫Dφ(y)[v]dν(y) = ∫ζ₀(dω(y))dν(y) = 0 by step 2. ∎

subproblem.title: Riesz vector of the wedge functional w ↦ ζ₀(w^♭∧α)
subproblem.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, ζ₀ ∈ Λ_{d+1}(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P (d+1), a continuous linear functional on (d+1)-covectors) and α a d-covector on ℝ^P. Then there is a vector v ∈ ℝ^P such that for every w ∈ ℝ^P and every (d+1)-covector γ with γ(u_0, …, u_d) = Σ_{i=0}^{d} (−1)^i⟨w, u_i⟩α(u_0, …, û_i, …, u_d) for all u (û_i omitted, i.e. α(Fin.removeNth i u)), one has ζ₀(γ) = ⟨v, w⟩. (Such a γ is w^♭∧α; v is the Riesz representative of the linear functional w ↦ ζ₀(w^♭∧α).)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (ζ₀ : MultiVector P (d + 1)) (α : Covector (Euclid P) d), ∃ v : Euclid P, ∀ (w : Euclid P) (γ : Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1)), (∀ u : Fin (d + 1) → Euclid P, γ u = ∑ i : Fin (d + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (i : ℕ) * (inner ℝ w (u i) * α (i.removeNth u))) → ζ₀ γ = inner ℝ v w
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 2 of the parent proof (the wedge w^♭∧α := exteriorDerivative (y ↦ ⟨w, y⟩•α) 0 and the Riesz vector v_α of w ↦ ζ₀(w^♭∧α)), with the uniqueness of w^♭∧α and its linearity in w written out. Uses the sibling extderiv_smul (accepted dgcr_bwd_extDeriv_smul_const): for a : ℝ^P → ℝ differentiable at x and a constant m-covector β, exteriorDerivative (y ↦ a(y)•β) x u = Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i·(Da(x)(u_i)·β(removeNth i u)) for all u : Fin (m+1) → ℝ^P.
Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with real inner product ⟨·,·⟩; a d-covector is an element of Covector (Euclid P) d (a continuous alternating d-linear form); ζ₀ ∈ MultiVector P (d+1) is a continuous linear functional on (d+1)-covectors; removeNth i u := Fin.removeNth i u; for w ∈ ℝ^P and u : Fin (d+1) → ℝ^P put F_w(u) := Σ_{i=0}^{d} (−1)^i·(⟨w, u_i⟩·α(removeNth i u)).
1. (The covector W(w) = w^♭∧α.) Fix w ∈ ℝ^P. The function a_w(y) := ⟨w, y⟩ is the continuous linear map innerSL ℝ w, so it is differentiable at 0 and its derivative there is innerSL ℝ w itself (ContinuousLinearMap.differentiableAt, ContinuousLinearMap.fderiv), i.e. Da_w(0)(h) = ⟨w, h⟩ (innerSL_apply_apply). Define the (d+1)-covector W(w) := exteriorDerivative (y ↦ ⟨w, y⟩•α) 0. By extderiv_smul with m = d, a = a_w, β = α, x = 0, for every u: W(w)(u) = Σ_i (−1)^i·(Da_w(0)(u_i)·α(removeNth i u)) = F_w(u).
2. (Uniqueness.) Let γ be a (d+1)-covector with γ(u) = F_w(u) for all u. Then γ(u) = W(w)(u) for every u by step 1, so γ = W(w), because continuous alternating maps with the same values are equal (ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext).
3. (W is linear in w.) Let w, w' ∈ ℝ^P and c ∈ ℝ. For every u, by step 1 and ⟨w + w', u_i⟩ = ⟨w, u_i⟩ + ⟨w', u_i⟩ (inner_add_left), W(w + w')(u) = Σ_i (−1)^i·((⟨w, u_i⟩ + ⟨w', u_i⟩)·α(removeNth i u)) = F_w(u) + F_{w'}(u) = (W(w) + W(w'))(u) (distribute each term and split the sum, Finset.sum_add_distrib); hence W(w + w') = W(w) + W(w') (ext). Likewise, by ⟨c•w, u_i⟩ = c·⟨w, u_i⟩ (real_inner_smul_left) and pulling the constant c out of the sum (Finset.mul_sum), W(c•w)(u) = c·F_w(u) = (c•W(w))(u); hence W(c•w) = c•W(w).
4. (The functional ℓ.) Define ℓ(w) := ζ₀(W(w)). Since ζ₀ is linear, step 3 gives ℓ(w + w') = ζ₀(W(w) + W(w')) = ℓ(w) + ℓ(w') and ℓ(c•w) = ζ₀(c•W(w)) = c·ℓ(w). So ℓ is a linear functional on the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P, hence a continuous linear functional (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap).
5. (Riesz representative.) Let v := (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ ℝ^P).symm ℓ, the Riesz representative of the continuous linear functional ℓ. Then ⟨v, w⟩ = ℓ(w) for every w ∈ ℝ^P (InnerProductSpace.toDual_symm_apply).
6. (Conclusion.) The vector v depends only on ζ₀ and α. Let w ∈ ℝ^P and let γ be a (d+1)-covector with γ(u) = Σ_i (−1)^i·(⟨w, u_i⟩·α(removeNth i u)) = F_w(u) for all u. By step 2, γ = W(w); hence ζ₀(γ) = ζ₀(W(w)) = ℓ(w) = ⟨v, w⟩ by step 5. This is the claim. ∎

  intro P d ζ₀ α
  set W : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1) :=
    fun w => exteriorDerivative (fun y => inner ℝ w y • α) 0 with hW
  have hWf : ∀ (w : Euclid P) (u : Fin (d + 1) → Euclid P), W w u = ∑ i : Fin (d + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (i : ℕ) * (inner ℝ w (u i) * α (i.removeNth u)) := by
    intro w u
    have hd : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun y => inner ℝ w y) (0 : Euclid P) :=
      (innerSL ℝ w).differentiableAt
    rw [hW, Submission.dgcr_bwd_extDeriv_smul_const P d (fun y => inner ℝ w y) α 0 u hd]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => ?_)
    have hf : fderiv ℝ (fun y => inner ℝ w y) (0 : Euclid P) = innerSL ℝ w :=
      (innerSL ℝ w).fderiv
    rw [hf, innerSL_apply_apply]
  have huniq : ∀ (w : Euclid P) (γ : Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1)), (∀ u : Fin (d + 1) → Euclid P, γ u = ∑ i : Fin (d + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (i : ℕ) * (inner ℝ w (u i) * α (i.removeNth u))) → γ = W w := by
    intro w γ hγ
    ext u
    rw [hγ u, hWf w u]
  have hadd : ∀ w w' : Euclid P, W (w + w') = W w + W w' := by
    intro w w'
    ext u
    rw [ContinuousAlternatingMap.add_apply, hWf, hWf, hWf, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => ?_)
    rw [inner_add_left]
    ring
  have hsmul : ∀ (c : ℝ) (w : Euclid P), W (c • w) = c • W w := by
    intro c w
    ext u
    rw [ContinuousAlternatingMap.smul_apply, hWf, hWf, smul_eq_mul, Finset.mul_sum]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => ?_)
    rw [real_inner_smul_left]
    ring
  let ℓ : Euclid P →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ :=
    { toFun := fun w => ζ₀ (W w)
      map_add' := by
        intro w w'
        simp only [hadd, map_add]
      map_smul' := by
        intro c w
        simp only [hsmul, map_smul, smul_eq_mul, RingHom.id_apply] }
  refine ⟨(InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (Euclid P)).symm (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap ℓ), ?_⟩
  intro w γ hγ
  rw [InnerProductSpace.toDual_symm_apply, huniq w γ hγ]
  rfl
proof_key_steps: W(w) := exteriorDerivative (y ↦ ⟨w, y⟩•α) 0 satisfies W(w)(u) = Σ_i (−1)^i⟨w, u_i⟩α(removeNth i u) (extderiv_smul with Da_w(0) = innerSL ℝ w), and every γ with this formula equals W(w) (ext).
W is additive and homogeneous in w (inner_add_left, real_inner_smul_left, ext), so ℓ(w) := ζ₀(W(w)) is a linear, hence continuous, functional on ℝ^P.
v := (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ ℝ^P).symm ℓ satisfies ⟨v, w⟩ = ℓ(w), so ζ₀(γ) = ζ₀(W(w)) = ℓ(w) = ⟨v, w⟩.
